newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: ALPINE SKIING-"TORNADO' TOMBA GETS VICTORY BOOSTER.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-"TORNADO' TOMBA GETS VICTORY BOOSTER.

text.p: Alberto Tomba powered to his first Alpine skiing World Cup victory of the season on Thursday, saying it made him feel like a tornado ahead of the world championships in Sestriere.
The Italian's triumph in a slalom under floodlights came with a fastest aggregate time of one minute 35.87 seconds on the Planai piste.
Tomba finished 0.16 seconds clear of Austria's Thomas Stangassinger and 0.31 in front of Frenchman Sebastien Amiez to give him a timely boost ahead of his home world championships starting on Sunday.
"Step by step I made it to the top of the podium again and just in time for the championships. It was very important for me to win a race before Sestriere. This gives me confidence," said Tomba.
"Now I have two weeks to continue preparing for Sestriere. I feel like a cyclone, no even better, I feel like a tornado.
"I started the second run with a lot of speed but made a mistake early on, so I decided to ski the middle section like an instructor. Then in the bottom half I just went for it again.
"It is increadible that I made it so far, considering all the problems I had over the past five months," said the Italian, who is also a triple Olympic champion.
Tomba missed the first few races of the season after injuring his knee and wrist in a heavy fall during training, while a bout of influenza slowed him down at the beginning of this month.
"Now I am back. In Kitzbuehl I was good but here I stepped up a gear," said Tomba, who was second behind Austria's Mario Reiter in last Sunday's Kitzbuehel slalom.
He is now eagerly anticipating the world championship slalom on February 15 which will also be raced under floodlights as well as the giant slalom.
The Italian is hoping to repeat his good performance from last year's world championships in Sierra Nevada, Spain, where he captured gold in both technical disciplines.
"Things look good in slalom. But I need more training in giant slalom," said Tomba, who has not made a single World Cup giant slalom appearance this winter.
He has competed in only four slaloms this season, finishing second in Madonna, eighth in Kranjska Gora and second in Kitzbuehel in the previous three.
Austria's Thomas Sykora defied a hip injury sustained in a heavy fall before the slalom in Kitzbuehel to improve on a first-leg ninth place for overall fourth (1:36.23).
Sykora has won five of the eight slaloms this season, finished second once and continues to lead the slalom World Cup standings on 666 points ahead of Stangassinger (490) and Amiez (328).
"I am happy Tomba won. Now he is the favorite for the Sestriere slalom," said Sykora. "This removes a lot of weight from my shoulders."
